references.text: God commands Israel to build a sanctuary so that he may dwell among them, which is the same promise of God's presence among his people.
God promises to set his dwelling place in the midst of Israel and walk among them; he will be their God, and they shall be his people.
Ezekiel prophesies that God's dwelling will be with them; he will be their God, and they shall be his people.
Zechariah prophesies that the Lord will dwell in the midst of Zion, many peoples will join themselves to the Lord, and he will be their God.
Paul quotes the promise that God will dwell among his people and walk among them; he will be their God.
John sees the fulfillment of the promise in the new Jerusalem, where God's dwelling is with humanity, he will live among them, and he will be their God.
The building of Solomon's temple fulfills the promise of God's presence given at the dedication of the tabernacle.
Leviticus elaborates on the conditions for the fulfillment of God's promise to dwell in their midst.
Zechariah confirms that God's presence among the people is central to the restoration of Jerusalem.
Uses the promise of God's presence as direct justification for the land's purity.
